data.body:
DECISION (operator-directed 2026-09-01): abandon this approach; do NOT land change 2483.

Rationale (grounded in ADR 0106 + epic 536b + a945's own scope and 2483's review history):

1. NO CUTOVER = NO BENEFIT. a945's scope explicitly excludes any live-store cutover
   ("Do not run this migration against the live shared .tickets-tracker; fixture/throwaway
   stores only"; "any live shared-store cutover are out of scope"). ADR 0106 defines W2's
   ENTIRE value as cutting ~270 KB/commit of root-tree churn ON THE LIVE STORE. Without the
   cutover, the churn bug is unresolved and the sharded layout is an unused parallel path.

2. THE CUTOVER IS NO-GO. Epic 536b (polite-antivirus-bedbug, the store-growth program that
   owns W1/W2/S1-S3) recorded pre-swap go/no-go = NO-GO for the live shared-store swap. So the
   cutover that would give W2 value is not on the table.

3. REVIEW FORCED THE MIGRATION INERT. Across 7 patch sets on change 2483 the LLM-Review gate
   forced ticket-layout-shards to become opt-in/inert-by-default (PS7: without an explicit
   typed config/env opt-in it "returns failed and leaves the store unchanged"). The landed
   result would be XL sharding machinery (a new _store/ticket_layout module + rerouting every
   ticket-dir call site + mixed flat/sharded readers) whose migration never runs on the live
   store.

4. NET: XL codebase complexity with zero delivered bug resolution. This is an approach
   previously rejected by the operator.

Action: Gerrit change 2483 abandoned; a945 closed as wontfix. If root-tree churn reduction is
revisited, it belongs under epic 536b's structural-lever program WITH a live cutover in scope
(currently NO-GO), not as a standalone cutover-less sharding task. The ~21h agent worktree
(/Users/joeoakhart/w2-shard-ticket-dirs, commits on Change-Id I2641612162199ae821d1df920e6e3290db34e731)
is discarded as worthless per this decision.
